title: Serve Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, a 2.4T-Parameter Model, with Configurable Reasoning on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Alibaba open-weighted Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, a 2.4T-parameter fine-grained MoE with 95B active parameters, a 1M-token context and hybrid full/linear attention, and NVIDIA claims Day-0 serving of over 4K tokens/sec/GPU and over 350 tokens/sec/user on GB300 NVL72 in FP8. NVIDIA's framing is that a model this size is unservable without rack-scale co-design — specifically the 72-GPU NVLink domain running all-to-all at 130 TB/s — with NVFP4 gains still to come.

themes.theme: Chinese open weights at near-frontier scale

insights.claim: Alibaba released open weights for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (Qwen3.8-Max), a 2.4T total-parameter model with 95B activated per token, putting near-frontier capability into the open ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Open weights at 2.4T compress the moat of closed frontier labs and shift value toward whoever owns the serving infrastructure — which is NVIDIA's implicit argument here.
insights.quote: Alibaba released the open weights for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (Qwen3.8-Max), its largest open-weight model, bringing near-frontier capabilities to the open ecosystem.

insights.claim: NVIDIA is actively working with the open-source ecosystem to bring a Chinese-origin frontier-scale model to multinode deployment via optimized kernels, inference runtimes, and distributed serving recipes.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is model-agnostic by design: every credible open model, regardless of origin, becomes a demand driver for its rack-scale systems.
insights.quote: NVIDIA is working with the open-source ecosystem to bring the model to multinode deployments through optimized kernels, inference runtimes, and distributed serving recipes.

themes.theme: Architecture built for agentic context growth

insights.claim: The model alternates full-attention layers with linear-attention layers that replace a growing KV cache with a bounded recurrent state, keeping both compute and memory bounded as context scales to one million tokens.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Hybrid attention attacks the KV-cache memory wall directly — a structural headwind to the thesis that long context linearly increases HBM demand per user.
insights.quote: In the full-attention layers, every token attends to every other token, and in the linear-attention layers, the growing KV cache is replaced with a bounded recurrent state.
insights.locator: The full-attention and linear-attention hybrid architecture

insights.claim: Agentic workloads differ from chat because they accumulate system instructions, tool outputs, retrieved documents, code, logs and multi-step reasoning traces across a workflow, making attention, compute and KV cache memory the binding constraints.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: The shift from chat to agents changes the hardware bottleneck from FLOPs to memory bandwidth and capacity — favoring HBM-heavy, high-interconnect systems.
insights.quote: As context grows, attention, compute, and KV cache memory become the binding constraints.

insights.claim: Fine-grained MoE distributes capacity across many small experts rather than few large ones, so serving cost tracks the 95B active parameters rather than the full 2.4T — delivering frontier-scale capacity at a fraction of the cost of a comparable dense model.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Parameter counts are decoupling from inference cost, so headline model size is no longer a reliable proxy for compute demand per token.
insights.quote: A learned router activates only the experts needed per token, so serving costs track active parameters, not the full 2.4T parameters, delivering frontier-scale capacity at a fraction of the cost of a comparable dense model.
insights.locator: Fine-grained MoE makes the 2.4T parameter count practical

insights.claim: Built-in low/high/xhigh reasoning controls let developers trade compute for reasoning quality per request, dialing up for multi-step reasoning or down for high-throughput document processing.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Per-request compute dials make inference spend elastic and controllable, which flattens the relationship between adoption growth and token spend.
insights.quote: Built-in reasoning controls (low/high/xhigh) enable developers to configure inference depth per request, trading compute for reasoning quality depending on the task

insights.claim: Without additional model tuning, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B hits over 4K tokens/sec/GPU and over 350 tokens/sec/user on GB300 NVL72 in FP8 precision on Day 0, with NVFP4 optimizations still expected to add gains.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Day-0 numbers this specific are the competitive benchmark rivals must beat; the reserved NVFP4 upside signals NVIDIA expects to raise the bar again without new silicon.
insights.quote: the model achieves a throughput of over 4K tokens per second per GPU and over 350 tokens per second per user on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 in FP8 precision on Day 0

insights.claim: The GB300 NVL72's 72-GPU Blackwell Ultra NVLink domain delivers all-to-all communication at 130 TB/s, which NVIDIA positions as eliminating the expert-routing bottleneck that appears when MoE traffic must cross off-the-shelf networks.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: The interconnect, not the GPU die, is the stated moat for serving large MoE models — the key line of defense against merchant accelerators and custom ASICs.
insights.quote: Its large, 72-GPU NVIDIA NVLink domain enables efficient all-to-all communication at 130 TB/s, eliminating bottlenecks that appear when expert traffic must cross traditional off-the-shelf networks.
insights.locator: The GB300 NVL72 features a rack-scale architecture

insights.claim: NVIDIA argues that inference at 2.4T-parameter scale depends on extreme co-design across chips, system architecture, and software, requiring data-center-scale accelerated compute rather than commodity nodes.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: The pitch reframes inference — historically the more contestable workload — as a rack-scale systems problem where NVIDIA's full-stack integration is hardest to unbundle.
insights.quote: Inference at this scale depends on extreme co-design across chips, system architecture, and software.

insights.claim: NVIDIA supports SGLang, vLLM and its own Dynamo as open-source inference paths for the model, plus a 'model-free' NIM container that serves any supported model — hedging across community runtimes rather than forcing its proprietary stack.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is conceding the runtime layer to open source while monetizing the hardware beneath it — the serving-software land grab is not where it is defending margin.
insights.quote: SGLang, vLLM, and NVIDIA Dynamo provide open-source inference recipes for developers who require greater control over performance on the NVIDIA-accelerated platform.
insights.locator: Post-train Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and choose a serving path

insights.claim: NeMo AutoModel offers PyTorch-native fine-tuning with Day-0 Hugging Face checkpoint support and full SFT or LoRA, training directly on existing checkpoints without model conversion.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Removing the conversion step lowers switching friction into NVIDIA's post-training tooling, extending lock-in above the driver layer.
insights.quote: Train directly on existing checkpoints without model conversion, with support for full SFT or memory-efficient LoRA fine-tuning.

insights.claim: Distribution for the weights runs through both Hugging Face and ModelScope, confirming the Chinese model-hosting channel as a parallel and equally supported release path.
insights.speaker: Amr Elmeleegy
insights.so_what: Two-hub distribution means model diffusion is not gateable at a single Western chokepoint — relevant to any export-control or platform-restriction thesis.
insights.quote: Download Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B model weights from Hugging Face or ModelScope and deploy with a model-free NVIDIA NIM from NVIDIA NGC.
